learning_outcomes.text: Adequate application of knowledge on energy conversion, electromagnetic and mechanical phenomena specific to static, electromechanical converters, electrical equipment and electromechanical drives
Identification of the objectives to be achieved, available resources, conditions to complete them, working stages, working times, associated deadlines and risks

Familiarization of the students with the field of electric drives. Theoretical and practical knowledge on the technique of electric drives is provided, as well as research, design and use of electric drive systems with DC and AC machines.
Present the theoretical elements of the technique of electric drives, electric drives with DC and AC machines

Familiarize students with practical aspects of the operation of the electric drive system, the control methods of electrical actions with DC and AC machines, including modern control methods with programmed logic and computer control.

syllabus_topics: Subject of electrical drives
Introduction in electrical drives with the presentation of the course with video projector, on the board or online
Structure and construction of electrical drive systems
General problems of electrical drives technology
The object of the kinematics and dynamics of electrical drives. Motion equation
Reporting of couples, moments of inertia, strength and mass
Mechanical characteristics of electric machines and working mechanisms
Transmission of the movement from the electric machine to the working mechanism. Electromagnetic couplings
Electrical drives with DC machines
Electrical drives with DC machines
Drives with permanent magnets direct current machines
Reversible drives with DC machines
Electrical drives with asynchronous machines
General relationships and mechanical features for electrical drives with asynchronous machines
Methods of starting for electrical drives with asynchronous machines
Braking methods for electrical drives with asynchronous machines
Speed control for electrical drives with asynchronous machines
Presentation of the laboratory, of the labor protection norms and of the conventional signs specific to the field of electric drives.
Methods and schemes for starting DC motors
Using the Simulink program to simulate DC motors with separate excitation drives
Methods and schemes for starting asynchronous motors
Presentation of the ASMA program used for computer simulation of asynchronous machine drives
Changing the speed of drives with asynchronous machines by changing the frequency of the supply voltage
Closing the situation at the laboratory.
teaching_methods: Presentation of the course with video projector
Presentation on the board or online
Theoretical test at the beginning of the laboratory
Practical part of the work under the guidance of the teacher

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory test + practical application (including laboratory work during the semester and laboratory work file)

assessment_rules: For the course exam, a minimum mark of 5 requires knowledge of fundamental notions without presenting details; for a mark of 10, thorough knowledge of all subjects is required. For the laboratory, a minimum mark of 5 requires recognition of the stands used for laboratory works; for a mark of 10, detailed knowledge of how to perform all laboratory work is required. Students receive a test and a grade at each laboratory, plus a grade for laboratory work during the semester and for the laboratory work file, which results in an average for the laboratory.
